text:
Jordan: Quick sync — I sketched a single-page failure-surface map for multi-site failover. High level: three independent dimensions we must own: control-plane RPCs (leases, routing decisions), data-plane inference traffic (active inference lanes + cache priming), and consent/audit propagation. Putting the diagram in drive: https://redwood/internal/drive/multisite/failure-surface.png. Want alignment before I turn this into a proper RFC.
Maya: link looks good, thanks. What's the ask here? a strawman for operator steps or just interface boundaries? :thinking:
Jordan: Both. I want to (1) call out exact RPCs that must be strongly consistent across sites, (2) enumerate degraded behaviours we accept per-surface, and (3) propose a test matrix.
Liam: First question — are we committing to active/active with per-tenant primary affinity, or active/passive warm-standby for some customers? The surface looks very different for each.
Jordan: Good call. My proposal: default active/active with primary-affinity hints (client-side header + control-plane lease). But allow a tenant-level mode: "local-only" that pins writes to region. Active/passive is only for tenants that explicitly opt-in to lower cost SLA (rare).
Sara: Data residency note: for tenants with residency flags we must ensure write telemetry and raw logs never leave the region unless explicitly allowed. That affects how we design audit propagation — we may need selective fanout instead of global replication.
Nina: Observability implication: traces must carry site tag and tenant residency flag so we can slice traces without reconstructing post-hoc. Also need cross-site span linking ID so a request that falls back to another site shows up as a single end-to-end trace.
Ethan: Operator/runbook corner: circuit boundaries. If a site becomes overloaded, we need a deterministic circuit that preserves legal requirements. For residency-locked tenants, circuit should return 429+residency-route header rather than failover. For non-residency tenants, failover is allowed.
Maya: Is there an agreed format for the control-plane lease RPC? I want to avoid a large migration later. Small proto sketch?
Jordan: Yeah — suggested proto is tiny: LeaseAcquire(tenant_id, preferred_site, ttl) -> LeaseToken(site, expires_at). We'll require idempotency key for retries. I'll add proto to the drive.
Liam: Tradeoffs: active/active means KV cache priming is hard (cold misses on new site). We could pre-warm popular prefixes via async mirror when we detect steady-state shift. But that introduces replication bandwidth. Thoughts?
Sara: For residency tenants we can't mirror raw KV. But we can mirror metadata/redirects and a small "consent stamp" so the other site can return a polite redirect. That keeps legal boundary intact.
Nina: Telemetry-wise we should capture cache-miss rates per-tenant-per-site and feed that to the routing-controller to bias affinity. Low-latency telemetry loop (1m buckets) should be enough.
Ethan: Testing matrix suggestion: (A) Chaos: site kill — assert SLOs for large-tenant set and residency tenants behave correctly. (B) Burst: cross-site burst and assert queueing/circuit behaviour. (C) Compliance: simulate EU tenant and ensure no payload leaves region.
Jordan: Agree. I'll draft the RFC with those tests and include the proto, operator runbook snippets, and a prioritized checklist for infra.
Maya: One more: client routing. We need a header that indicates "prefer-local" vs "require-local". Clients should be able to opt into either for each request. This avoids per-tenant toggle for simple cases.
Liam: Implementation detail: prefer-local header can be advisory — control-plane may ignore if primary overloaded. require-local must be enforced by proxy (401/451/429 depending).
Sara: Also call out retention/replication of audit logs — retention controller must be region-scoped for residency tenants. Add that as a MUST.
Nina: For observability, we should define a single metric name for "cross_site_failover" with labels {tenant, from_site, to_site, reason}. Makes dashboards consistent.
Ethan: Operational note: add a preflight operator check that verifies no live tenants are in migration during cutover experiments. The preflight should fail if >0 migrations in last 15m.
Jordan: Great — I'll update the diagram and PR the RFC draft tomorrow morning. Quick asks before I write it up: any missing surfaces?
Maya: Maybe data-plane device attachments (GPUs) and cold-queue priming — how we track model weights prefetched per-site. Could be a separate surface but worth calling out.
Liam: One more: backup and sweep — if we failover writes temporarily, how do we reconcile conflicts? Need a conflict policy appendix (last-writer-win vs vector clocks) per-data-type.
Jordan: Noted. I'll include a compatibility table: inference requests (idempotent) vs metadata writes (CRDT/merge) vs billing events (append-only).

Sara: thanks — nice to have a canary while we iterate on the RFC.
Jordan: Thanks all. I'll tag owners on the RFC draft and schedule a 30m sync after the draft lands. :eyes:
